# SplatKit — Camera Plot Flythrough (End User Guide)

## Overview

This workflow turns a **single 360° panorama** into a **COLMAP / SfM dataset** for 3D Gaussian Splatting. It does this by generating several **camera-path flythroughs** through the scene: each camera plot renders a geometry-based control video from the panorama, drives a **Wan 2.1 I2V** generation along that path, and the resulting panoramic frames from every plot are fused into one SphereSfM dataset.

**Input:** one equirectangular panorama (e.g. `pano_360_*.png`).
**Output:** generated flythrough videos per camera plot **+** a reconstructed COLMAP dataset ready for splatting.

### Color legend (how to read the canvas)

| Zone color | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **White / Grey** | Model loaders, project setup, and the COLMAP dataset builder |
| **Green** | Your inputs (panorama image, prompts, steps) |
| **Purple** | The camera plots — one group per camera path |

---

## Required Custom Nodes

| Node Pack | Used for |
|-----------|----------|
| **ComfyUI-SplatKit** | All `SplatKit_*` nodes: `DatasetProject`, `CameraPlotRenderControlGeo`, `WanI2VMaskedConditioning`, `SphereSfMDataset`, `SphereSfMAddToDataset`. |
| **Mickmumpitz-Nodes** | The on-canvas title labels. |

Everything else (loaders, KSampler, VAE Decode, Create/Save Video) is **built-in ComfyUI**.

---

## Required Models

See the orange **Model download links** cards to the right for exact URLs and target folders.

| Model file | Loader | Purpose |
|------|--------|---------|
| **Wan2_1-I2V-14B-720P_fp8_e4m3fn.safetensors** | UNET Loader | Main image-to-video model. |
| **umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors** | CLIP Loader (type `wan`) | Text encoder. |
| **clip_vision_h.safetensors** | CLIP Vision Loader | Image conditioning. |
| **wan_2.1_vae.safetensors** | VAE Loader | Encode / decode latents. |
| **pano_video_gen_720p_comfy.safetensors** | LoRA (strength **0.98**) | Panoramic video LoRA — keep enabled. |
| **lightx2v_..._distill_v2_lora_rank64_bf16.safetensors** | LoRA (strength **1.00**) | Step-distill LoRA for fast few-step sampling. |

---

## 1. Load the Models

In the grey **LOAD DIFFUSION MODELS** zone, load the six models above. Both LoRAs are pre-wired — leave the strengths as set (**0.98** pano, **1.00** lightx2v).

## 2. Project Setup (green **SETUP** zone)

1. **Panorama** — load your 360° equirectangular image in the `Load Image` node.
2. **Dataset Project** (`SplatKit_DatasetProject`) — set the project name (e.g. `warm-throneroom-02`). This one field drives all the output folders and control-frame prefixes automatically; nothing is hardcoded to your machine.
3. **Prompts** — a positive prompt describing the scene and a negative prompt for quality.
4. **STEPS** — sampling steps (shared by every camera plot). With the lightx2v LoRA this stays low (default **8**).

## 3. Camera Plots (the purple groups)

Each **purple group is one camera path**. Inside a group:

- **Camera Plot / Render Control Geo** — paste the camera path (one keyframe per line: `x, y, z` positions, optionally with a `look-at` target) and choose the look mode (`look_forward`, `per_point_look`, …). It renders the control video + mask from the panorama geometry.
- **Wan Conditioning** → **KSampler** → **VAE Decode** generate the flythrough along that path.
- Two **Save Video** nodes preview the **control** pass and the **final** generated pass.

You can **duplicate** a group to add another path, **mute** a group to skip it, and **rename** it. Every group reuses the same models, prompts and steps, so you only edit the camera path per group.

## 4. Create the COLMAP Dataset (white **CREATE COLMAP DATASET** zone)

`SplatKit_SphereSfMDataset` collects the initial panorama plus the generated frames from every camera plot and builds a **SphereSfM / COLMAP** dataset. `SplatKit_SphereSfMAddToDataset` can append an extra camera path to an existing dataset. The result is ready for downstream 3D Gaussian Splatting.

---

## Recommended Order

1. Load the six models.
2. Set the **Dataset Project** name and load your **panorama**.
3. Write the **prompts** and confirm **STEPS**.
4. Define each **camera path** in the purple plots (duplicate / mute as needed).
5. Run — each plot renders its flythrough and everything is fused into the COLMAP dataset.
